A systematic review and meta-analysis published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2010 examined the HIV status in discordant couples in sub-Saharan Africa, highlighting the importance of targeted interventions in this population. 2. The World Health Organization (WHO) released guidance in 2012 on couples' HIV testing and counseling, including the use of antiretroviral therapy (ART) for both treatment and prevention in serodiscordant couples, emphasizing a public health approach. 3. Hagan et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in 2011, published in The Journal of Infectious Diseases, to evaluate interventions aimed at preventing hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection among people who inject drugs. 4. In 2013, the WHO published a report addressing responses to intimate partner violence and sexual violence against women, providing recommendations for healthcare systems to better support affected individuals. 5. Chou et al. in 2012, under the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force, provided recommendations for preventive services, emphasizing evidence-based approaches to improve healthcare delivery. 6. A study by Chen et al. in 2010, published in the International Journal of STD & AIDS, found that Australian men who have sex with men preferred rapid oral HIV testing over conventional blood testing, suggesting the need for more accessible testing options. 7. Johnson et al. in 2017 conducted a systematic review on the issue of poor-quality HIV testing and misdiagnosis, published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society, underscoring the need for improved diagnostic accuracy in public health systems. 8. Wilson et al. in 2019 performed a scoping review on HIV retesting policies, practices, and behaviors in lowand middle-income countries, published by the WHO, to inform strategies for improving retesting rates. 9. Wringe et al. in 2017 explored the experiences of HIV testing and their implications for patient engagement in care and treatment, as part of a multicountry qualitative study published in Sexually Transmitted Infections. 10. The WHO in 2018 emphasized a public health approach to ensuring quality HIV testing in the context of antiretroviral drug use, advocating for standardized procedures and ethical practices. 11. In 2016, the WHO released guidelines on HIV self-testing and partner notification as a supplement to its consolidated guidelines on HIV testing services, promoting innovative approaches to expand testing coverage. 12. Fox et al. in 2016 conducted meta-analyses on interventions to improve the rate and timing of ART initiation for HIV in sub-Saharan Africa, published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society, demonstrating the effectiveness of targeted strategies. 13. The WHO's 2019 consolidated guidelines on HIV testing services highlighted the importance of focusing on undiagnosed individuals and linking them to care and treatment services as early as possible. 14. The WHO recommends integrating HIV testing services with other health services, such as tuberculosis, viral hepatitis, sexually transmitted infections, and reproductive health services, to minimize missed opportunities for diagnosis and care. 15. Task sharing and the use of trained lay providers are encouraged to expand HIV testing services, particularly in community-based settings, to reach underserved populations effectively. 16. The WHO updated its recommendations in 2016 to include HIV self-testing as an approach to HIV testing services, emphasizing the need for community engagement in developing and adapting self-testing models. 17. Social network-based HIV testing approaches are recommended by the WHO as part of a comprehensive care and prevention package for key populations, with a focus on identifying undiagnosed infections. 18. The WHO's 2019 guidelines stress that HIV testing services must adhere to the 5 Cs—Consent, Confidentiality, Counseling, Correct test results, and Connection to care and treatment—to ensure ethical and effective service delivery. 19. HIV self-testing does not provide a definitive diagnosis; individuals with reactive results must undergo confirmatory testing by trained providers using verified national testing algorithms. 20. Integration of HIV testing with other health services aims to make testing more convenient, reduce missed opportunities, and improve client satisfaction while addressing co-infections and other health conditions simultaneously. 21. The WHO emphasizes the importance of timely linkage to prevention, treatment, and care following HIV testing, as testing without appropriate follow-up services is not beneficial. 22. Strategies to expand HIV testing services include decentralization, task sharing, and integration with other health services to improve accessibility, efficiency, and cost-effectiveness. 23. Integrated service delivery can reduce duplication, improve coordination, and enhance the overall efficiency of health systems, benefiting both clients and healthcare providers.
